title: Comparative efficacy of tool-augmentation versus constrained decoding for preventing high-risk semantic misconfigurations under adversarial intents (repaired/preregistered)
research_question: Under adversarial or out-of-distribution intent prompts, does tool-augmentation (generate→validate→repair) reduce high-risk semantic misconfigurations relative to LLM-only generation in vendor-specific intent→configuration pipelines?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: Tool-augmented pipelines (generate→validate→repair) produce a lower high-risk semantic failure rate than LLM-only generation (paired comparison).

H2: The absolute reduction in high-risk semantic failure rate between tool-augmented and LLM-only pipelines is at least 5 percentage points (the primary minimum-detectable-effect used for sample-size justification).
exploratory_questions: E1: How do failure-mode frequencies (ACL, routing, interface/address overlap, BGP/neighbor misconfig) differ between pipelines?
E2: Does constrained/grammar-aware decoding (not available as a confirmatory adapter) offer complementary benefits when combined with tool-augmentation? (exploratory descriptive analyses only)
benchmark_scope: Public vendor-configuration corpora and intent→configuration pairs derived only from redistributable public datasets referenced in the supplied evidence records (e.g., W4415124495, W4400072049). Non-redistributable items will be redacted and replaced prior to release; all retained items will be hashed and archived.
model_scope: Single hosted LLM provider endpoint (preregistered model_name and model_version below). All model calls through the hosted-model API available in the frozen capability manifest; no local GPU execution.
Deterministic decoding parameters (temperature, top_p, seeds) frozen in preregistration.
transformation_scope: baseline: direct_configuration_generation_v1 (LLM-only output given an intent).
guarded: generate_validate_repair_v1 (LLM generation followed by deterministic validators; if validator fails, a single automatic repair-generation call is attempted, then validator re-run).
primary_estimand: Paired absolute difference in high-risk semantic failure proportions (LLM-only minus tool-augmented) across the predeclared task sample, estimand computed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor (estimand id: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline).
secondary_estimands: Per-vendor paired absolute differences (Cisco IOS, Juniper Junos).
Repair success rate: proportion of initial-validator-failed tasks where a single automated repair produces a validator-pass.
Failure-mode relative-frequency differences by category (ACL, routing, neighbor, interface/address).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired design using the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Primary confirmatory sample size: task_count = 600 paired tasks chosen deterministically using the adapter's challenging_workflow_stress_v1 profile (task_indices generated by the adapter index rule). Episodes_per_task = 2 (baseline and guarded). Final per-adapter model-calls = task_count * 2 = 1,200. Task selection is outcome-independent and fixed before any model calls.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor runs McNemar-style paired comparison (as implemented by paired_binary_analysis_v1) of binary final semantic-pass outcomes (validator pass/fail) between baseline and guarded conditions, reporting absolute risk difference and 95% CI (Clopper–Pearson style for proportions as provided by the executor). Secondary analyses: pairwise descriptive comparisons, stratified vendor estimates, failure-mode frequency tables with Fisher-exact tests (Bonferroni-corrected for the number of secondary tests), and bootstrap CIs for repair success rates. Report both primary-complete analysis and a sensitivity analysis that treats technical model-call failures as failures (failed_call_treatment options exercised). All analysis will be performed by the provided paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor (compatible with the available adapters).
multiplicity_plan: Primary hypothesis (H1/H2) is single confirmatory test. Secondary and exploratory tests are explicitly labeled exploratory; p-values reported with Bonferroni correction across the family of secondary tests. No multiplicity correction applied to exploratory descriptive charts; all exploratory inferences are clearly marked as such.
missingness_plan: Technical model-call failures or adapter errors: primary analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary' treatment (pairs with technical infrastructure failures are excluded from the confirmatory test and reported with counts and reasons). Sensitivity analysis will use 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' treating technical failures as semantic failures. All failure counts and their locations (initial generation vs. repair attempt) will be logged and reported.

benchmark_names: Public NetOps config corpora referenced in supplied evidence (see evidence_record_ids list)
Adversarially perturbed-intent set (algorithmically generated; redacted on public release per safety policy)
risk_factors: Pre-lock development artifacts accidentally reused as evidence (policy prohibits use).
Leaked or redistributability-restricted vendor configs included by mistake.
Adversarial-intent exemplars exposing exploit payloads in public artifacts.
detection_procedures: Automated provenance check: every dataset item must include a public-source URL and license tag before inclusion; otherwise it is excluded or redacted.
Hash-based duplication detection vs. archived pre-lock artifacts to ensure no pre-lock development payloads are used.

Automated redaction filter applied to adversarial examples: replace potentially harmful substrings (per regex rules) with <REDACTED> before any public release; full hashed artifacts retained in a restricted archival bundle but not published.
item_flagging_rules: Flag any dataset item lacking a public license or source for removal.
Flag adversarial examples containing explicit exploit strings (pattern list) for redact-only release.
Flag validator-detected ambiguous ground-truth configurations for additional automated consistency checks; such items are excluded from confirmatory sample if consistency checks fail.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Flagged/contaminated items are excluded from the confirmatory primary analysis; exclusions listed with counts and reasons. Sensitivity analyses will (1) include flagged items with conservative redactions where safe and (2) report confirmatory results both with and without flagged items.
residual_uncertainty: Deterministic validators may not capture some real-world semantic failures; sensitivity analysis and error taxonomies mitigate but do not eliminate this residual uncertainty.
Public dataset representativeness of production configurations remains limited (external-validity limitation).

budget_scenarios.description: Primary recommended scenario balancing power, model-call budget, and runtime feasibility: N=600 paired tasks evaluated with hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (baseline vs guarded).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: task_count*2=600*2=1,200 model calls matches the adapter's maximum_model_calls rule and lies well below the capability manifest maximum_planned_model_calls=10000. Wall-clock execution feasible within the 7-day limit given minimal per-call reasoning effort and one repair call per failed initial candidate at most.

budget_scenarios.description: Higher-powered scenario to detect smaller differences: N=1,250 paired tasks (exploratory if resources permit).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: task_count*2=1,250*2=2,500 model calls; still ≤ capability manifest model-call budget (10000) and compatible with hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter limits. Recommended only if additional API budget and time are provisioned; otherwise use scenario_A_recommended.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Paired absolute difference in semantic-failure rate (guarded minus baseline).
power_plan.target_effect: Detect an absolute difference of 5 percentage points (e.g., baseline 10% → guarded 5%) with power ≥ 80% at α=0.05 under conservative variance assumptions.
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate normal-power calculation using paired-difference approximations and conservative independence-biasing assumptions; solved for sample sizes at common assumptions (see assumptions).
assumptions: Baseline semantic high-risk failure rate ~10% (conservative operational estimate derived from evidence-synthesis gaps).
Target guarded failure rate ≤5% (absolute reduction of 5 percentage points).
Paired design reduces required sample versus independent-group assumptions; calculations use conservative variance estimates to avoid under-powering.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=600 paired tasks, the design has ≈80% power to detect an absolute difference ≈5 percentage points under the above assumptions. Detecting a 4 percentage-point difference would require ~720 pairs; scenario_B (N=1250) increases sensitivity and precision.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute paired analysis under alternative baseline failure-rate assumptions (5%, 10%, 15%).
Treat technical failures as semantic failures in a sensitivity run (conservative bound).
Bootstrap CI estimation of the absolute risk difference.

transformation_families: Grammar-aware parsing and syntax checks (vendor-specific CLI grammars).
Semantic validators (ACL semantics, routing table consistency, neighbor/BGP/OSPF config checks, interface/address overlap detection).
Automatic repair-generation (single LLM repair attempt guided by validator error messages).
semantic_equivalence_checks: For repair outputs, re-run the deterministic semantic validators; only validator-pass outputs are accepted as final-pass.

For a 100-item seeded synthetic test-suite with known injected faults, measure validator sensitivity/specificity vs injected ground-truth labels (no human adjudication required because injected faults are algorithmically known).
automatic_rejection_rules: If vendor-grammar parsing fails, the pipeline performs no further automatic rollout and marks the task as validator-fail; the repair attempt is still executed (per adapter policy) but failed parses are flagged and excluded from any public example dumps.

If validator reports any 'critical' class error (predefined list: ACL deny-all mispolicy insertion, overlapping addressing that would blackhole prefixes, BGP neighbor-deletion), the final output is rejected (counts reported); no human adjudication.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Algorithmic audit: create a 100-case seeded synthetic fault corpus (covering each error type) and measure validator detection rates (sensitivity, specificity). Audit executed automatically; results reported in manuscript.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: All configuration and grammar artifacts are hashed and archived. Only configurations with public redistributable licenses are retained; non-redistributable items are redacted and replaced. Mapping from intents→configs uses deterministic templates; mappings are verified by replaying templates on a 200-example holdout to confirm parser acceptance rates ≥95%.
residual_risks: Validator false negatives for novel semantic errors not represented in the seeded audit suite.
Incomplete vendor grammar coverage leading to parse-acceptance bias.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: External validity: public corpora and simulated validator checks may not fully capture the diversity of production device configurations and operational policies (bounded claim to public/simulated benchmarks).
Residual validator coverage: despite algorithmic audits, validators may miss rare semantic failure modes not represented in the seeded fault set.

Constrained/grammar-aware decoding is not available as a confirmatory adapter in the frozen adapter contract; results about constrained decoding will be exploratory/qualitative rather than the preregistered confirmatory estimand.
